schema_ddl:
CREATE TABLE PARTS (PNUM INT, QOH INT);
CREATE TABLE SUPPLY (PNUM INT, SHIPDATE INT);
q1: SELECT X.PNUM AS XP FROM PARTS AS X WHERE (X.PNUM, X.QOH) IN (SELECT Y.PNUM, COUNT(Y.SHIPDATE) AS CNT FROM SUPPLY AS Y WHERE Y.SHIPDATE < 10)
q2: SELECT X.PNUM AS XP FROM PARTS AS X, (SELECT Y.PNUM AS SUPPNUM, COUNT(Y.SHIPDATE) AS CT FROM SUPPLY AS Y WHERE Y.SHIPDATE < 10 GROUP BY Y.PNUM) AS TEMP WHERE X.QOH = TEMP.CT AND X.PNUM = TEMP.SUPPNUM
q1_prompt_sql: SELECT X.PNUM AS XP FROM PARTS AS X WHERE (X.PNUM, X.QOH) IN (SELECT Y.PNUM, COUNT(Y.SHIPDATE) AS CNT FROM SUPPLY AS Y WHERE Y.SHIPDATE < 10)
q2_prompt_sql: SELECT X.PNUM AS XP FROM PARTS AS X, (SELECT Y.PNUM AS SUPPNUM, COUNT(Y.SHIPDATE) AS CT FROM SUPPLY AS Y WHERE Y.SHIPDATE < 10 GROUP BY Y.PNUM) AS TEMP WHERE X.QOH = TEMP.CT AND X.PNUM = TEMP.SUPPNUM
explanation: Q1 and Q2 are not equivalent. Q1 selects parts where (PNUM, QOH) matches a tuple from a subquery that counts SHIPDATE for each PNUM in SUPPLY with SHIPDATE < 10. Q2 matches parts where QOH equals the count of SHIPDATE (i.e., the count of supply records) for each PNUM in SUPPLY with SHIPDATE < 10. These are fundamentally different conditions.
counterexample_dsp: A simple case where a part has a QOH equal to the number of supply records for that part with SHIPDATE < 10 will show differences in behavior between the two queries.
